title: Musette in D major
short: Anonymous (long credited to J. S. Bach) · D 2/4 · listen, then play it.
trouble: Reading notes one at a time instead of in chunks.

blocks.html: A musette is a dance named after a small bagpipe, and the left hand imitates its drone by jumping between low and high D. In bars 3 and 4 both hands play the same notes, two octaves apart. Bars 5 to 8 repeat the opening, and each half of the piece is played twice.
What to notice: Musette, BWV Anh. 126, from the Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach (1725)

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys light up, and “wait for me” lets you practise one hand at a time.

items: both hands playing the same notes

blocks.html: Play through it once with the right hand only, then add the left. Which chord change made you stop?

sources.name: Mutopia Project edition of BWV Anh. 126 (Allen Garvin, from the Bach-Gesellschaft edition; public domain), compared with this file note by note by our checking script. IMSLP notes that Bach’s authorship is uncertain.
